_exec_summary.SummaryText:
Sika Corporation
Dallas Operations
13524 Welch Road, Dallas, Texas, 75244
RMP Executive Summary

Accidental Release Prevention & Emergency Response Policies

We are submitting an updated Risk Management Plan (RMP) to reflect a technical change in our covered process: replacing the currently registered blowing agent (n?pentane) with a blended mixture of iso?pentane and normal (n?) pentane. Under 40?CFR?68.190(b), any change that introduces a regulated substanceor modifies the quantity presentabove threshold limits in an existing covered process requires submission of a revised RMP within six months. Since the iso?pentane/n?pentane blend meets those criteria, we are required to resubmit accordingly. All  sections of the RMP have been fully updated to incorporate the new substances characteristics in line with regulatory requirements.

Blended pentane agents (n?pentane with iso?pentane) are widely used within the insulation and polyurethane foam industries to optimize performance characteristics. This change is driven by both regulatory commitment to efficiency and our companys goal of delivering higher-quality, energy-efficient products. The physical, safety, and handling properties of the iso?pentane/n?pentane blend are similar to those of the previously used n?pentane, ensuring that existing controls and emergency response plans remain appropriate and effective.
No new hazards have been introduced, and current mitigation strategies continue to adequately manage risk.

Sika's management, at both the plant and corporate level, is extremely committed to the safety and health of its employees, contractors, and visitors, and to minimizing to the greatest extent practicable the potential for releases which may adversely affect the environment. This commitment is a critical element of the facility's RMP/PSM Plan. It will extend not only through the initial development of the plan, but will endeavor to incorporate the practices and procedures established by this plan in

. In the unlikely event the containment wall fails to restrict a chemical spill, Sika certified HAZMAT technicians may be asked to place absorbent barriers in the flow path of the spilled chemical. However, Sika employees will not be asked to make contact with hazardous spilled chemicals.       
 
Facility & Regulated Substances Handled

Sika, Dallas Operations manufactures polyisocyanurate foam insulating board (foam board). The facility operates under the North American Industrial Classification System (NAICS) Code 32615 (Urethane and other foam (except polystyrene) manufacturing). The foam board produced at the facility is used in both residential and commercial construction applications. Sika produces foam board in thickness ranging from ½ inch to 4.5 inches.

Sika uses three main raw materials in the production of foam board: Methylene diphenyl diisocyanate (MDI), Polyol, and Blowing Agent (Pentane Blends).  Several catalysts and fire retardants may also be used depending upon the type of foam board being produced. MDI is considered as part A and Polyol combined with catalyst and surfactants are considered as a part B.   

The main raw materials are all liquids and are stored on-site in bulk tanks of 9,500 gallons and 12,000 gallons. The liquids flow through a series of tanks, static mixers and high-pressure pumps towards the pour table. At the pour table, parts A and B are combined together and injected between the top and bottom facers. Sika uses several different types of facers, depending upon the type of foam board being produced. Once parts A and B are combined the liquids exothermically react to form solid foam. 

Isopentane (CAS No: 78-78-4) is a substance regulated by 40 CFR 68 [EPAs Chemical Accident Prevention Provisions]. Taking into account 40 CFR §68.115(b)(2)(i), Sika has determined the total quantity of Pentane in its foam board manufacturing process (for purposes of a threshold quantity determination) to be the total amount of the Hydrocarbon B

lowing Agent present in its process at any one time. The maximum amount present in Sika's foam board manufacturing process at any one time is 56,700 pounds. This is above the threshold quantity for Pentane of 10,000 pounds, as established in 40 CFR §68.130. Therefore, Sika has determined that the Dallas facility is subject to the requirements of 40 CFR §68 for Pentane. 

Sika has defined its covered process as that equipment which contains or contacts the Hydrocarbon Blowing Agent starting at the bulk storage tank loading (or fill) connection and extending up to and including the mix heads (located at the Pour Table). This determination was made based on the fact that once the Blowing Agent is mixed with the other foam components; it is no longer a liquid and is part of a solid, non-flammable product.  Thus, the blowing agent is flammable according to the definition as contained in 29 CFR §1910.1200(c). As stated previously, the Sika Dallas Operation may have up to 56,700 pounds of Hydrocarbon Blowing Agent present in its process at any one time. This is above the applicability quantity for a flammable liquid of 10,000 pounds, as established in 29 CFR §1910.119(a)(1)(ii). Thus, Sika has determined its Dallas, Texas facility is subject to the requirements of 29 CFR §1910.119.

Through preparation of this Risk Management Program / Process Safety Management Program (RMP/PSM), Sika has determined that its Dallas Operation is a Program 3 process as defined by 40 CFR §68.10(d). This determination is based on the results of the worst-case release scenario for n-Pentane (the location of public receptors being within the distance to the endpoint) and the applicability of 29 CFR §1910.119 to its facility. Thus Sika has complied with the requirements for preparation and submittal of a Program 3 RMP as contained in 40 CFR §68.

Worst Case and Alternative Release Scenarios

In order to calculate the distance to the endpoint from a worst case release of Blowing Agent (Isopentane

blends), the EPA automated program RMP*Comp browser based version was used to perform the off site consequence analysis. The program provided a conservative estimate for the distance to an endpoint of 1.0 psi overpressure. The quantity of n-Pentane used in the worst case release scenario analysis for Sika's Dallas, Texas facility has been determined to be the amount of Blowing Agent contained in the facility's on-site bulk storage tank. In accordance with 40 CFR §68.25(e), for purposes of calculating the distance to the worst case release endpoint, Sika has assumed that the entire contents of the single largest vessel containing Blowing Agent (56,700 pounds) is released as a vapor, which finds an ignition source, and that 10% of the released quantity participates in the resulting explosion. 

Sika has determined the maximum threat distance to an endpoint of 1.0 psi overpressure using RMP*Comp is 0.3 miles for a release quantity of 56,700 pounds of Blowing Agent.  Using U.S. Census Data for 2020 and an aerial map, it is estimated there is a residential population of approximately 1,200 within a 0.3 mile radius.  The vast majority of the affected area is occupied by industrial and commercial properties.  Sika has determined, through examination of the Addison USGS 7.5 Minute Topographic Quadrangle Map, that there are no environmental receptors located within the 0.3 mile radius.

Sika has identified another possibility for the release of Blowing Agent that is more likely to occur than the worst case release.  This possible alternative release scenario was defined as a 10-minute transfer hose release of Blowing Agent during tanker truck unloading.  Sika has determined, based on the physical properties of the Blowing Agent, that a release from a transfer hose would result in a spill of a highly volatile liquid which would have the potential to result in a Pool Fire. 

Sika has determined the maximum threat distance to an endpoint of 5 kilowatts per square meter [as spec

ified in 40 CFR 68.22(a)(2)(ii)] using RMP*Comp is 0.06 miles for a release quantity of 16,183 pounds of Blowing Agent.  Using U.S. Census Data for 2020, it is estimated there is less than 2 persons within a 0.06 mile radius.  The affected area is 100% occupied by industrial and commercial properties.  Sika has determined, through examination of the Addison USGS 7.5 Minute Topographic Quadrangle Map, that there are no environmental receptors located within the 0.06 mile radius.
